items.s: Please reply today. This matter is ____ and cannot wait.
Before an exam, many students feel ____ and cannot sleep.
It is hard to ____ on your homework when your phone keeps buzzing.
Going to bed early and eating breakfast are healthy ____.
Your ____ is the way your body breaks down the food you eat.

match.d: to get back to normal after a hard time
awake and ready to notice things
facts that show that something is true

items.s: In October 2026, The Guardian ____ experts whether any of this is true.
When you are stressed, your heart ____ faster.
Dr Lai ____ breathing in for about five seconds.
In one study, the breathing exercise ____ people's mood over a month.
The "rest and digest" mode ____ down your heart.

tfn.s: The experts say that you would not want a nervous system reset.
tfn.why: The text says: "There is no such thing as a nervous system reset, and you would not want one."

tfn.s: Dr Lai suggests slow breathing for only about one minute.
tfn.why: The text says: "breathing in for about five seconds and out for about five, for five to ten minutes"

tfn.s: One expert says there is not enough good evidence for the benefits of cold water.
tfn.why: The text says: "there is not enough good evidence that it gives real benefits for the nervous system"

tfn.s: The text says that the stress response is never useful.
tfn.why: The text says: "That is useful, because you need it to exercise and concentrate."

tfn.s: The text says how many people took part in the cyclic sighing study.
tfn.why: The text does not say how many people took part in the cyclic sighing study.

pre.d: to set something back to how it was at the start
to say that something will definitely happen
a way that something works
full of energy and unable to relax
the way you feel at a particular time
proof or help that shows an idea is good
quick jumps into very cold water
taking air in and out of your body

focus.note: Some words always take the same small word after them. Learn the pair together, not the small word alone.

items.s: It can take a few minutes to recover ____ a stressful day.
How much sleep you need depends ____ your age.
If you feel low for a long time, talk ____ a doctor.
Many people are interested ____ new ways to relax.
Some people are afraid ____ very cold water.
The wellness ____ sells many products that promise quick results.
Early nights and regular meals may sound ____, but they help more than most gadgets.
She slept for twelve hours because she was so ____ after the marathon.
A ____ bedtime matters more than one long lie-in at the weekend.
The shop sells a wide ____ of products, from herbal teas to sleep masks.
Your muscles ____ when you feel threatened.

match.d: the loss of a person close to you through death
able to be believed or trusted
to relax and become calm after being busy or stressed
to recover quickly after a difficulty

items.s: By the time the meeting ended, Sam ____ at his desk for nine hours.
The feature ____ on 2 October 2026.
Over the last few years, slow breathing ____ to raise heart rate variability.
If she ____ more, she would feel less wired.
If you enjoy it and feel calmer, he ____, that is reason enough.

tfn.s: Every expert agreed that the nervous system cannot be reset.
tfn.why: The text says: "Every expert agreed that there is no such thing as resetting the nervous system"

tfn.s: The experts say the stress response is always harmful.
tfn.why: The text says: "That response is useful, because we need it to exercise, concentrate and meet deadlines."

tfn.s: The text suggests that more exercise is always better for the nervous system.
tfn.why: The text says athletes who overtrain show lower heart rate variability, "so recovery matters".

tfn.s: The neurosurgeon says cold water has clear and proven benefits.
tfn.why: The text says: "there is not yet enough credible evidence of meaningful benefits for the nervous system"

tfn.s: The text says how many people took part in the cyclic sighing trial.
tfn.why: The text does not say how many people took part in the cyclic sighing trial.

pre.d: able to be trusted to work well
a sore, swollen, red area in the body
helping to cause something
to do too much exercise without enough rest
again and again, without stopping
not working in a balanced way
important enough to make a real difference
popular at a particular time

focus.note: Many verbs and adjectives need one particular preposition. Check the pair in a dictionary and learn it as one chunk.

items.s: Researchers often rely ____ heart rate variability as a measure of calm.
Regular exercise can contribute ____ better recovery over time.
Many people benefit ____ a short walk after lunch.
Some influencers are accused ____ exaggerating the effects of simple tricks.
It is hard to cope ____ stress without a break.
Where the supply of skilled staff ____ behind demand, wages tend to rise.
A hibernating animal ____ energy by slowing almost everything its body does.
Researchers recorded each volunteer's resting pulse as a ____ before the programme began.
The company's shares dipped on Monday, but a strong ____ on Tuesday wiped out the loss.
The appeal of the scheme is ____: it saves money and it saves time.
She is an ____ authority on sleep research, quoted in many journals.

match.d: an idea that an argument is based on
something used to stand for another thing that is hard to measure

items.s: The review reported a ____ increase in heart rate variability, but not that it lasted.
Specialists remained ____ of any claim that promised an instant fix.
The ____ of the trial was limited because only a short period was studied.
Overtraining without enough rest can lead to a ____ in performance.
It would be ____ to conclude that a better reading means a better health outcome.

tfn.s: The review found that slow breathing raised heart rate variability only during a session, not afterwards.
tfn.why: The text says it was higher "during a session, immediately afterwards and after multi-session programmes".

tfn.s: The evidence for acupressure mats is weaker than the evidence for slow breathing.
tfn.why: Slow breathing "has the clearest support", while evidence for acupressure mats "is thinner still".

tfn.s: The text says consumer vagus nerve devices have been proven not to work.
tfn.why: The text says the evidence is limited, "which is not the same as proof that they fail".

tfn.s: The review found that slow breathing worked better in younger people than in older people.
tfn.why: The text does not say anything about age in the review.

tfn.s: The text suggests that a better heart rate variability reading does not by itself prove a health benefit.
tfn.why: The text says "a better reading on it is not the same as a proven health benefit".

pre.d: not working in a steady, balanced way
working automatically, without you thinking about it
the act of putting the whole body into water
doing too much exercise without enough rest
ordinary and not exciting
not the same in every part or case
worried or badly affected by a problem
the facts and conditions around a situation

focus.note: At this level the preposition often belongs to a fixed phrase, so learn each one as a whole chunk with an example.

items.s: Promising an instant cure is tantamount ____ misleading the public.
The success of the programme is contingent ____ people sticking to it.
Early attempts to measure calm were fraught ____ difficulty.
The claim is ____ odds with all the available evidence.
The programme succeeded by virtue ____ its simplicity.

speak.title: Role-play: is the mat worth it?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the flatmate who wants to buy
a.text: You saw a video about a spiky mat that promises to calm you down. It costs a lot. Explain why you want it and try to persuade your flatmate to share the cost.

b.text: You are not sure the mat is worth the money. Ask about the evidence, suggest a cheaper idea and try to agree on a plan you are both happy with.

phrases: I saw a video that says it works in five minutes.
That's a lot of money for a mat.
I'd rather try something free first.
Let's wait a week and then decide.
I'm not convinced, but I'm happy to try.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you buy the mat, and why?
